THE STATE OF GOA & ORS. RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The dispute pertains to selection for the post
of Coach (Grade-IV) in weightlifting in the State of
Goa. In the course of the selection process, a
dispute arose as to the fairness of the selection
process, upon which the appellant raised a complaint
before  the  Competent  Authority  of  the  State
Government, leading to a direction to re-conduct the
tests.
3. Thereafter, respondent No. 4 preferred a Writ
Petition in which the impugned order has been passed
without impleading or affording any opportunity of
hearing to the appellant.
4. Considering that the appellant and respondent
No. 4 are the only two candidates competing for the
post, we deem it appropriate to direct the High Court
1

--- Page 463 ---
to  decide  the  matter  afresh  after  affording  an
opportunity of hearing to both parties. Consequently,
the  impugned  order  is  set  aside,  and  the  Writ
Petition preferred by respondent No. 4 is restored to
its original number for a decision afresh on merits
upon  hearing  all  parties  to  the  Writ  Petition,
including  the  present  appellant  who  shall  be
impleaded as a party before the High Court.
5. We request the High Court to decide the matter
at the earliest. The interim order passed by this
Court shall remain in operation during the pendency
of the Writ Petition.
6. It is made clear that the High Court shall not
be influenced either by its own previous order or by
this order, and the matter shall be decided afresh on
its own merits.
7. The appeal is disposed of in the above terms.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA 
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.          OF 2026
[arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 13497 OF 2026]
HARSHVARDHAN KUMAR MEENA                          APPELLANT
                                VERSUS
STATE OF RAJASTHAN                                  RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur, by the
impugned judgment and order dated 22nd May, 2026, has dismissed
the appellant’s application for bail.
3. Appellant was arrested on 6 th March, 2024 in connection with
FIR No. 0010 of 2024 dated 3 rd March, 2024 registered at Police
Station (SOG),  District – ATS and SOG for the offence under Sections
419, 420, 408, 409, 467, 468, 471, 477, 477-A, 201, 109 read with
Sections 34 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860; under
Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the Rajasthan Public Examination
(Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 1992
and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and
perused the materials on record.
5. Insofar as the claim of parity raised by learned counsel for the
appellant is concerned, we find that this Court has granted the relief

--- Page 467 ---
2
of bail to the appellant’s co-accused. Significantly, the kingpin -
Jagdish Vishnoi - has also obtained enlargement on bail from the
High Court itself and this Court, in its jurisdiction under Article 136 of
the Constitution of India, has spurned the challenge laid to such
order by the State in its special leave petition. Appellant is not
differently placed and, therefore, is entitled to claim parity.
6. That apart, the trial is likely to be a protracted exercise having
regard to the number of witnesses proposed to be examined by the
prosecution to drive home the charges against the appellant and his
co-accused.
7. Taking an overall view of the matter, we are of the considered
opinion that the appellant need not be detained in custody any
longer and that he could be admitted to an order for release on bail
pending trial.
8. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.
9. Appellant shall be released on bail, subject to furnishing of bail
bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to such other
terms and conditions as may be imposed by it.
10. Needless to observe, the appellant shall not, directly or
indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any
person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such
facts to the court.
11. In the event there is any breach of the terms and conditions

--- Page 468 ---
3
for grant of bail, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of
the appellant.
12. It is also ordered that the appellant shall diligently attend
proceedings of the trial, unless exempted. If he abstains from
attending the proceedings without justifiable cause, that could also
be seen as breach of the conditions for grant of bail and the trial
court will be free to pass appropriate orders.
13. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant
of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
14.  The appeal is, accordingly, allowed on the aforesaid terms.
15.  Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

[DIPANKAR DATTA]
……………..............................J.

1.   Leave granted.

High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Bench at Gwalior has rejected the
appellants’ prayer for bail in anticipation of arrest.  
3. Appellants figure as accused in FIR No. 0005/2026 dated 4 th
January, 2026 registered with Police Station-Kotwali, District-Seopur.
It is alleged in the FIR that the appellants have committed offences
punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of Madhya Pradesh Freedom of
Religion Act, 1968.

well as the respondent.
1 Criminal Case No. 18255 of 2026

--- Page 471 ---
2
5. It is not in dispute that the appellants, in terms of an earlier
order dated 31st August, 2026, have joined investigation. 
6. In such view of the matter, we are of the opinion that custodial
interrogation of the appellants is not necessary and that they may be
admitted to an order for grant of bail in anticipation of arrest.
7. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order stands set
aside.
8. It is directed that in the event of the appellants being arrested
in connection with proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR,
he/she  shall  be  released  on  bail  by  the  arresting/investigating
officer/trial court on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial
court.
9. It is made clear that in the event the appellants breach any of
the terms and conditions imposed by it, the trial court shall be at
liberty to cancel the bail of the appellants.
10. Needless to observe, the appellants shall not, directly or
indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any
person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such
facts to any police officer or to the court.
11. Also, since the investigation is yet to conclude, we direct that if
the  investigating  officer  calls  upon  the  appellants  to  join  the
investigation, he/she shall do so by attending the police station.
12. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of

NATIONAL HEALTH INSTITUTE AND
 MEDICAL RESEARCH CENTRE    PETITIONER(S)
                                VERSUS
MAX HEALTHCARE INSTITUTE LIMITED                   RESPONDENT(S)
(IA No. 230357/2026 - APPROPRIATE ORDERS/DIRECTIONS
IA No. 195118/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
IA No. 195116/2026 - STAY APPLICATION)
 
Date : 07-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SATISH CHANDRA SHARMA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NONGMEIKAPAM KOTISWAR SINGH
For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Bansal Charu Subhash- 4278, AOR 
                   
For Respondent(s) :Dr. S Muralidhar, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Raunaq Kamath, Adv.
                   Mr. Divyanshu Rai- 3166, AOR
                   Mr. Siddharth Varshney, Adv.
                   Mr. Yash Raj, Adv.
                   Ms. Ninni Susan Thomas, Adv.
                   Ms. Megha, Adv.
                   Mr. K. Rigved Prasad, Adv.
                   Ms. Apoorva Singh, Adv.                 
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Dr. S. Muralidhar, learned senior counsel appearing
for the respondent, initially argued the matter at length
before this Court, opposing the transfer of the suit, being
CS (COMM) No. 127 of 2026, titled “Max Healthcare Institute
Limited v. National Health Institute & Medical Research
Centre”, pending before the District Judge (Commercial
Courts), South District, Saket Complex, New Delhi, to
TRANSFER PETITION(S)(CIVIL)  NO(S).  1960/2026

--- Page 545 ---
2
Commercial Court No. 1, Jaipur Metropolitan-II, Jaipur,
Rajasthan.  He  placed  reliance  upon  the  order  dated
30.09.2013 passed in  M/s. Mac Charles (I) Ltd. v. M/s.
Indian Performing Rights Society Ltd. , SLP (Civil) No.
39994 of 2012.
2. While arguing the matter, learned senior counsel has
also placed reliance upon Section 142 of the Trade Marks
Act, 1999, and argued that the question of transferring the
aforesaid suit from the District Judge (Commercial Courts),
South District, Saket Complex, New Delhi, to Commercial
Court No.1, Jaipur Metropolitan-II, Jaipur, Rajasthan, does
not arise. After relying upon the order passed in M/s. Mac
Charles (I) Ltd. (supra), learned senior counsel sought
indulgence to place reliance upon another judgment before
this Court. The Court granted indulgence and passed over
the matter.
3. Upon the matter being taken up again, learned senior
counsel drew the attention of this Court to the order dated

NATIONAL RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT

O R D E R
1. Exemption application is allowed.
2. Leave granted.
3. The appellant preferred an application under Section 36
of the Arbitration Act, seeking stay of the Arbitral Award
passed by the Sole Arbitrator.
4. The High Court has directed the appellant to deposit
the entire decretal amount along with up-to-date interest,
within a period of four weeks with the Registry of the High
Court and subject to such deposit of the amount, the Award
would  remain  stayed  from  its  operation,  execution  and
enforcement.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would
submit that instead of asking the appellant to deposit the
entire decretal amount with the Registry of the High Court,
the appellant is ready and willing to furnish running bank
guarantee of a nationalized bank, of the decretal amount.
1

--- Page 569 ---
6. We modify the impugned order passed by the High Court
to the extent that it shall be open for the appellant to
furnish running bank guarantee of a nationalized bank of the
decretal amount, with interest as on date, with the Registry
of the High Court.
7. The running bank guarantee shall be furnished within a
period of four weeks from today, failing which, it shall be
open for the Award holder to proceed further with the
execution of the Arbitral Award.
8. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands disposed of.
9. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1947, as applicable to
Gujarat, it is claimed by the respondents that the present proceedings have

keeping all points open.

amendment, more particularly insertion of sub-section (4) of Section 9 in the
said Act, he shall be at liberty to challenge the judgment(s) and order(s) dated
14th July, 2026 and 23 rd July, 2026 once again in a freshly filed special leave
petition.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The  petitioner  has  approached  this  Court  being
1

--- Page 608 ---
aggrieved by an order passed by the High Court of Delhi at
New Delhi in W.P.(C) No. 19811 of 2025, declining to grant
interim relief.
3. The facts of the case reveal that the petitioner,
who was suffering from Alcohol Dependency Syndrome, Acute
Pancreatitis, and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, was discharged
from service vide order dated 31.12.2025.
4. The petitioner challenged the said discharge order
by filing an Original Application before the Armed Forces
Tribunal (AFT) along with a prayer for interim relief. The
AFT declined the prayer for interim relief.
5. Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner preferred a writ
petition before the High Court.
6. The High Court declined to grant interim relief on
the ground that the grant of interim relief would virtually
amount to granting the final relief itself.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has
contended before this Court that interim relief can be
granted even if it amounts to granting final relief,
placing reliance on a decision of this Court in Beg  Raj
Singh v. State of U.P. and Others  (decided on 18.12.2002).
The said judgment arose in the context of the grant of a
mining lease and does not advance the petitioner's case.
8. In light of the principles enunciated by this Court
in Deoraj  v.  State  of  Maharashtra  and  Others1, this Court
does not find any reason to grant interim relief to the
1 . (2004) 4 SCC 697
2

--- Page 609 ---
petitioner.
9. The Special Leave Petition is accordingly dismissed.
10. The petitioner shall be at liberty to argue the
matter finally before the Armed Forces Tribunal, where the
substantive Original Application is pending adjudication.
11. The Armed Forces Tribunal is requested to decide the
pending matter at an early date, as expeditiously as
possible.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Pursuant  to  our  order  dated  16.09.2026,  a
compliance affidavit has been filed.
2. Besides,  a  copy  of  the  order-sheet  of  the
proceedings under Section 12 of the Protection of
1

--- Page 617 ---
Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (for short
‘D.V. Act, 2005’) of the case concerned has been
placed before us.
3. A perusal of the order-sheet would reveal that
Section 12 proceedings were instituted on 26.08.2022.
Notices were issued fixing 30.11.2022 for appearance
of  the  respondent  in  those  proceedings.  On
30.11.2022,  without  recording  any  satisfaction
regarding service of notice on the respondent, the
order-sheet records that fresh steps are to be taken
fixing 21.03.2023.
4. It is further reflected from the order-sheet
that on 22.12.2022, the record of the case was put up
before  the  concerned  Magistrate  along  with  an
application under Section 19 of the D.V. Act, 2005.
On that date, the respondent-husband was restrained
from dispossessing the aggrieved person from shared
household till disposal of the case. Further, he was
restrained from alienating the shared household. The
order mandates that its copy must be served to the
aggrieved person free of cost. It was also directed
that  a  copy  of  the  order  be  also  sent  to  the
Inspector-In-Charge of Chakdaha Police Station for
information.
5. The  sale  deed  in  question  was  executed  on
23.12.2022 after the injunction order was passed.
However, there is nothing on record to indicate that
2

--- Page 618 ---
the party against whom the injunction order was
passed  was  either  served  with  notice  of  the
proceedings  or  had  entered  appearance  in  those
proceedings. Besides, the order-sheet reflects that
the date fixed in those proceedings vide entry dated
30.11.2022 was 21.03.2023, and fresh steps were to be
taken for service. In such circumstances, it is clear
that when the sale deed in question was executed, the
husband was not aware of the injunction operating
against him. Consequently, the respondent/ purchaser,
who was dispossessed pursuant to the order of the
learned Magistrate, in our view, was justifiably
directed to be put back in possession by the impugned
order of the High Court.
6. Accordingly, these Special Leave Petitions are
dismissed.
7. Dismissal of these petitions shall be without
prejudice to the rights of the petitioner to seek
recourse to other remedies against the husband in the
proceedings under the D.V. Act, 2005.
8. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.            
(CHETAN ARORA)                                  (SAPNA BANSAL)

2. Having considered the matter in its entirety, we find that the
present Special Leave Petition is not maintainable, as it arises
from an order passed in review proceedings pursuant to a remand by

--- Page 671 ---
2
SLP (C) D. No. 58439/2026
against the first impugned order dated 09.04.2024 passed by the
High Court.
3. Even otherwise, having considered the matter, we do not find
any  error  in  the  impugned  order  dated  03.09.2026  warranting
interference by this Court.
4. However, learned Senior Counsel points out that an amnesty
scheme is in vogue, which requires the proceedings to be pending,
and that, with the conclusion of the present proceedings, the right
even to apply under the scheme may be foreclosed.
5. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner fairly submits that
he has already applied, but has the apprehension that it may not be
considered on account of the conclusion of these proceedings.
6. Having regard to the aforesaid, we make it clear that the
scheme under which the petitioner has applied shall be considered
notionally as on the date on which it was filed, with regard to the
facts existing as on that date, and the present dismissal will not
have any adverse effect on the said proceedings.
7. Accordingly, the Special Leave Petition stands dismissed.

condonation of delay stands disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the
parties and having gone through the materials on record, we
find no error, not to speak of any error of law in the
impugned  order  passed  by  the  High  Court.  However,
1

--- Page 685 ---
considering the fact that this is a litigation between two
brothers, they should sit, talk and try to resolve the
matter.
2. We take notice of the fact that the suit is of the
year 2017. Almost 19 years have elapsed. Till this date,
even issues have not been framed. This is going to be a
never ending litigation.
3. We believe that the parties should go for mediation or
they should on their own try to resolve this controversy.
4. Parties may make all possible efforts to resolve the
dispute, failing which, the concerned Civil Court shall see
to it that the issues are framed at the earliest and the
suit is disposed of within a period of one year from today,
more particularly keeping in mind that the petitioner is 66
years old and the mother of the petitioner, who is one of
the defendant in the suit is a 90 year old lady.
5. The suit shall be decided on its own merits, without
being influenced in any manner, by any of the observations
made by the High Court in its impugned order.
6. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
7. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

For Respondent(s)  
   UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We are not inclined to interfere with the impugned admission
order passed by the High Court, as Section 100(5) of the Code of
Civil Procedure, 1908, leaves it open to the petitioner, Vrindavan
Chaturvedi, to raise the question as to whether the substantial
1

--- Page 813 ---
questions of law, as framed, would actually arise for consideration
in the appeal. Further, the proviso thereto makes it clear that the
questions of law framed at the time of admission would not be
binding upon the Court at the stage when the main appeal is heard.
That being so, we find no reason to condone the delay and
entertain this special leave petition. 
Accordingly, the applications for condonation of delay as well
as the special leave petition are dismissed. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 2005/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 19-12-2025
in CRLA No. 500/2003 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Bombay at Aurangabad]
DHANRAJ                                            Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF MAHARASHTRA                               Respondent(s)
(IA No. 38997/2026 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTS/FACTS/
ANNEXURES)
 
Date : 07-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJEEV SACHDEVA
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Sudhanshu S. Choudhari, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Siddharth S. Chapalgaonkar, Adv.
                   Ms. Sneha Sanjay Botwe, AOR
                   Mr. Akash Tripathi, Adv.
                   Ms. Aanchal Rathore, Adv.                   
For Respondent(s) : 
                   Mr. Varad Kilor, Adv.
                   Mr. Siddharth Dharmadhikari, Adv.
                   Mr. Aaditya Aniruddha Pande- 3259, AOR
                   Mr. Shrirang B. Varma, Adv.                   
          UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
I.A. No. 310319/2026 was filed by the learned counsel for the
State of Maharashtra, whereby the original and the translated
copies of the dying declaration of the victim were produced.
Perusal thereof reflects that the translated version of the
said dying declaration filed by the petitioner, at page 47 of the
1

--- Page 937 ---
SLP(Crl.) No. 2005/2026
special leave petition paper book, was materially altered. Question
No. 13 therein was as to how the victim was burned and scalded and
her answer, as reproduced at page 49, was to the effect that only
her mother-in-law and father-in-law were responsible.
However, the original and translated versions of the same,
filed by the learned counsel for the State, indicate that the
mother-in-law and father-in-law were stated to have poured kerosene
over the body of the deceased victim and it was the husband,
presently the sole petitioner herein, who set her on fire by
lighting a matchstick. His role was conveniently left out in the
translated version filed in the special leave petition.
In the light of the above facts, which clearly demonstrate
that the dying declaration was projected incorrectly before this
Court so as to secure interim relief in the form of exemption from
surrendering,  an  order  that  was  passed  as  long  back  as  on
30.01.2026, the special leave petition is liable to be dismissed
straightaway on account of this patent abuse of process by the
petitioner.  The same is, accordingly, dismissed.
Exemption from surrendering shall stand vacated. The State
shall take immediate steps to apprehend the petitioner so that he
can serve out the sentence imposed upon him.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(DEEPAK GUGLANI)                                (PREETI SAXENA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Heard Mr. Sridhar Potaraju, learned senior counsel
appearing  for  the  petitioner  and  Mr.  Devadatt  Kamat,
learned senior counsel appearing for the respondent-State.
By the impugned order, the High Court has relegated
the petitioner to Endowments Tribunal under Section 83(6)
of  the  Andhra  Pradesh  Charitable  and  Hindu  Religious
1

--- Page 1087 ---
Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987. The High Court has
also given a period of four weeks from 10.09.2026 to avail
the appellate remedy.
We are not inclined to interfere with the order
relegating the petitioner to alternative remedy. However,
considering the overall facts and circumstances and the
issues involved, we direct that in the event of any adverse
order passed by the Endowments Tribunal, the same will not
be given effect to for a period of 15 days from the order
of the Endowments Tribunal.

exercise jurisdiction under Section 9 of The Arbitration and

of the parties seeking to settle the dispute of its proceedings
through its process of mediation. The amount deposited before this
Court shall be transferred with interest to the execution Court
which shall be disbursed after its final decision.

the  Execution  Court  to  decide  the  issue  in  question  as
expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of six months
from today.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. On the suggestion from both sides, the impugned judgment of
the High Court dated 08.10.2025 is modified only to the extent that
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Jayant Nath, a former Judge of the High Court
of Delhi, is hereby appointed as the sole Arbitrator.
2. The learned Arbitrator shall commence the proceedings from the
stage of final arguments, for which the parties may be given one
opportunity to submit their written submissions followed by oral
submissions. Thereafter the learned Arbitrator shall proceed to
pass an appropriate award.
3. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
4. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
